verdict.rationale: Ubuntu Desktop's docs say it is a primary platform for major IDEs and that each release ships the latest applications, libraries and toolchains. Those are only general platform availability and package installation (adjacent features). Nothing documents a feature for quickly provisioning preconfigured development environments for specific frameworks or languages. The Amazon WorkSpaces mention is a third-party hosted offering, not a capability of the product itself.

support.subject: As a developer, I can quickly set up preconfigured development environments for popular frameworks and languages
